rows.what: Adds a warm edge glow to skin materials, a fake subsurface warmth. It does this by text-replacing chunks of three.js's built-in toon shader at compile time, using its own varyings and its own program cache key.

rows.evidence: TECHNICAL.md:44 (onBeforeCompile string-injects uRimColor/uRimStr/uRimPow; GLSL inside JS strings) and TECHNICAL.md:219 (that GLSL breaks naive brace counting in tools). No measurement recorded.
rows.v2_note: Avoid: patching shader text by string. It is a silent no-op if three.js renames a chunk, and WebGPURenderer node materials have no GLSL onBeforeCompile path at all, so any rim effect must be written in TSL or the new material system. `_matSig` (shamble-core.js:356) never shares a material that has this hook, so every skin part stays its own draw call. Learn: the self-contained varyings and the program cache key were what kept the hack stable on r128.

rows.what: Every outlined mesh gets a child copy drawn back-face-only in flat ink. A small vertex shader pushes it outward by a fixed width in world units and clamps it above the ground, so each object also gets an ink contact line where it meets the ground. Character parts get 0.8x the width.

Code: mergeStaticGroup counts 2 draw calls saved per merged mesh that has a hull (shamble-core.js:387 `saved+=(b.meshes.length-1)*(b.th>0?2:1)`), so a hull doubles each mesh's draw calls. reports/2026-10-16-three-teams-core-steps-1-6.md:57: the outline is lost on the very dark Empire coat (about 5 % luminance against a 15-25 % target).
rows.v2_note: Known cost: one extra draw call and one ShaderMaterial per outlined mesh. This feeds the 120-per-soldier risk (STATUS.md:84), which matters at LOOP_V2's 48-player scale. The GLSL ShaderMaterial does not run on WebGPURenderer (it needs TSL). Learn: world-unit width independent of scale, and the ground clamp that gives the contact line. Whether v2 inks at all is for the look brief.

rows.what: Precomputes, per geometry, a smoothed and mitred push direction for each vertex, so outline shells close at hard corners and keep a constant width. Results are cached by a content hash, so identical part shapes are solved once.
rows.where: shamble-core.js:310 `_oNCache` (Map, cleared entirely above 4000 entries at :344); :311-332 `_outlineDirs(P,N,n)` (sort by quantised position, sum distinct normals, scale 1/min(cos) capped at 2x); :333-347 `ensureOutlineNormals(geo)` (FNV-style position+normal hash, sets attribute `oNormal`). Callers: addHull (:393) and shamble-editor.js:877 and :882 (resize paths).
rows.evidence: TECHNICAL.md:47 describes the mitre capped at 2x and the 4000-entry cache cap. TECHNICAL.md:50: about 33 ms once at boot, about 1 ms per soldier (re)build, nothing per frame (measured headless).
rows.v2_note: A pure geometry algorithm with no per-frame cost. Learn: content-keyed caching made soldier rebuilds cheap. Weak spots: the cache drops everything at once past 4000 entries, and a geometry swapped in without this call silently falls back to plain normals (TECHNICAL.md:49). Uses `hyp3` (shamble-core.js:744). It is useful only if the look brief keeps hull outlines.

rows.system: userData tag contract between builders and the look pipeline
rows.what: The silent contract that decides how every mesh is styled and merged: builders set userData tags (matKind picks the cel ramp, outlineW the ink weight, part makes it a character part at 0.8x ink, noOutline skips the hull, nature bakes the environment brightness gain, noMerge keeps a collider body out of the static merge), and the pipeline sets its own (isOutline on every hull, _toon once a mesh is converted). A missing or misspelt tag fails silently: the mesh just gets the default ramp, the world ink weight, or a hull it should not have.
rows.where: Set by builders: matKind shamble-core.js:687 (buildEntity, from the recipe's mat role) and :754 (_gunParts); outlineW :686, :716 (makeAMKRifle), :755; part :686, :716, :753, shamble-game.js:1200 ('jug'); noOutline :276 (villain visor), :689 (copied from a recipe part's noOutline, e.g. :482), :716, :755; nature :230 (sea), :284, :1414, :1417, shamble-game.js:3070; noMerge shamble-game.js:577, :583, :598. Set by the pipeline: isOutline :395 (addHull); _toon :384 (merged mesh), :415 (stylizeOne). Read: matKind :404, :415; outlineW and noOutline :405, :416; part :392 (CHAR_OUTLINE multiplier); nature and baseCol :221 (applyEnv re-tint), :284; noMerge :364; _toon :413; isOutline :271, :364, :366, :386, :401, :413, :646 (applyFaction), shamble-game.js:245, :2573, shamble-editor.js:814, :877, :882.
rows.evidence: Code read (grep of each tag across the three engine files at 48ffb51). No measurement recorded. Related real bugs come from the stylize pass, not the tags themselves (CL8: PR #8 editor Ctrl+Z losing ink; parked bots left unstyled in 3a).
rows.v2_note: Learn: per-mesh intent (material kind, ink weight, skip outline, environment-only brightening, keep out of merge) is real data the look needs. Avoid: carrying it as untyped, optional userData strings that a later sweep reads, with no check that a builder set them; a typo or missing tag shows only as a wrong look. In v2, if the look brief keeps any of these, they belong as typed fields on the builder's output (or the material key), set where the mesh is built. Ties CL4 (toonify reads matKind and nature), CL6 (addHull reads part), CL8 (stylize reads noOutline and outlineW, sets _toon) and CL9 (merge reads isOutline and noMerge).
rows.reason: Look pipeline (styling inputs): redesign (look brief pending), with no further recommendation.

rows.what: A law-of-cosines two-bone solver: given a shoulder (or hip), a target, a pole direction and two bone lengths, it sets the upper bone's quaternion and the elbow (or knee) bend, clamping reach so the limb never locks straight. It uses preallocated scratch vectors (zero allocation) and serves both arms and legs.

rows.system: ASCII grid map format and parser (Cabana Republic)
rows.what: Cabana Republic is drawn as a 41 x 29 ASCII grid of 10 m cells, one character per cell for road, crate, building, barracks, silo, tech point and harvest field. parseGridToMapDef turns that grid into the same map-definition object buildMap uses. Team comes from which half of the grid a cell is in, and the spawn and resupply points are placed 15 m and 7 m from the friendly barracks, toward the centre. Crate cells carry a 'warm' tint flag, alternated by (r+c)&1, which buildMap turns into one of two crate materials. DM_Cabana is also the game's hard-wired default map: the harvester field, tech-box pool and silo pool are seeded from it at load, placeObjectives falls back to its field, tech points and silos when a map lacks them, boot builds it unless ?map=tri, and the editor's Reset rebuilds it.

rows.system: Cabana map content: spawn-side platforms and ramps, and the village pass
rows.what: An inline function adds three stepped platforms (1.2, 2.5 and 4 m) and ramps beside the friendly spawn, plus a ramp onto the lowest friendly base building's roof. The village pass is plain data: 11 houses, 70 trees, 36 props and 10 cover runs, designed as the left half and mirrored for team symmetry. The parser also writes Cabana's environment block (fog from 260 to 760 m) into the map, which map load hands to the shared environment code.

rows.system: Procedural canvas skins and the BK texture cache
rows.what: Ten functions each paint a 256 x 256 canvas texture (half-timber, terracotta tile, plaster, thatch, brick-and-flint, brick, slate, drystone, hedge leaves, dirt) with nearest filtering and repeat wrapping. BK.tex caches one shared copy per skin, with that skin's repeat.
rows.where: shamble-core.js:987 genTimberTex · 1009 genTileTex · 1049 genPlasterTex · 1056 genThatchTex · 1104 genBrickFlintTex · 1265 _bkBrickTex · 1271 _bkSlateTex · 1279 _bkStoneTex · 1286 _bkHedgeTex · 1291 _bkDirtTex · 1321-1327 BK.tex (cache _tex, repeat table)
rows.evidence: reports/2026-10-14-editor-undo-ground.md: the manor framing differs from run to run on both builds (unseeded house textures; 'house-textures-seeded' is queued, low priority, STATUS:30). Same report, PERF-2 (deferred, STATUS.md:97): _disposeObj3D disposes the shared cached BK textures; houses and covers already did on base, and trees and props now add the well roof's tile texture, so r128 re-uploads it next frame (1 extra 256 x 256 upload per rebuild; editor-undo-ground.md:51-53). ART_DIRECTION.md:127 and TECHNICAL.md:250: the brick-and-flint banding reads as 'candy stripes'. Code read: the legacy makers call genXTex() directly rather than BK.tex, so the 10 non-manor Cabana houses build 20 textures of their own.
rows.v2_note: Keep the technique: no external assets, painted procedurally, cached once per skin. Fix in v2: seed every painter (9 of the 10 use Math.random; genTileTex, core:1009-1022, is already deterministic; the kit already has _mulberry32) so renders and A/B shots are exact. Route every caller through the cache. Never dispose cached textures on teardown. NearestFilter, the 256 px size and the palettes are look choices, so they wait for the look brief.
rows.reason: Client-side procedural builders worth keeping in shape (code technique only, appearance pending).

rows.what: Five roof shapes built as non-indexed geometry, so every face gets a flat normal for crisp cel shading: gable (with a shifted ridge for saltbox), hip, half-hip, and gambrel. _roofFor turns the ridge to run along the building's longer side and adds the overhangs.

Roofs are not in collision or line of sight today (see CM13); a true 3D sim (VISION_V2 §6.2) will need roof volumes or walkable roofs.

rows.system: Building kit schema, presets and seeded roll

BK.roll uses a seeded mulberry32 generator to roll a full, resolved spec from a preset, so a placed building never reshuffles.

It returns the group, one local box collider per block (walls height) and the main wall mesh. It touches no game state.

rows.what: Turns a building's local-space collider boxes into world-space axis-aligned boxes using the group's transform, reusing the same Box3 objects after the first call. The manor, kit buildings and the editor's move and rotate call it. The SIM (shots and line of sight) reads those boxes (syncSimWorld game:1458). Movement reads them only for unrotated houses; resolveObstacles (game:2526) tests a rotated house against its localColliders in the house's own frame, an oriented test.

STATUS risk R1 (STATUS.md:108): rotated colliders at odd angles leave up to 0.34 m of solid inside free nav cells (editor-made maps). STATUS health (STATUS.md:118): syncSimWorld 561 B per call from the houses fallback array (team-prep-fixes PERF-4, :101).
rows.v2_note: Keep: local colliders plus a transform, recomputed without allocating. Avoid: an axis-aligned box of a rotated box (loose at odd angles). v2 should keep oriented boxes or convex volumes in the sim, as CS10's rayStatic already does for crates. Houses collide only up to wall height (roofs and chimneys are not solid); VISION_V2 §6.2 (floors, interiors, sight across heights) needs real volumes.
rows.reason: Static collision volumes belong to the authoritative v2 simulation.

rows.what: The hit volume of every soldier is one head sphere plus two vertical capsules (torso and legs). BODY copies the default character recipe's hit block, and the code comment claims one source for model and hitbox. In fact the same numbers are written twice (CHAR_DEFAULT.hit and _BODY_HIT, which the male and female base bodies use), and resolveShot tests every soldier against BODY whatever its recipe. A crouch offset would lower all three volumes, but it never applies.

rows.system: Ray versus sphere and capsule primitives
rows.what: Pure maths that returns the distance at which a ray first touches a sphere or a capsule, or -1 for a miss. A ray that starts inside the sphere returns 0. The capsule test falls back to its end spheres when the hit lands beyond the segment.
rows.where: shamble-core.js:1484 raySphere(ox..dz,cx,cy,cz,r); :1485 rayCapsule(ox..dz,ax..az,bx..bz,r) (closed-form infinite-cylinder test plus end-cap spheres; when the ray is parallel to the capsule axis, or the axis has zero length, it falls back to the two end spheres). Only callers: resolveShot core:1498, :1500, :1502.
rows.evidence: none recorded in any report. No report tests these two primitives on their own. The B7 parity test (reports/2026-10-15-team-prep-fixes.md:58) covers statics only. Node check on the real code (core:1484-1485 extracted): a horizontal ray that starts inside the torso cylinder (0,1.2,0) returns -1, a ray that starts inside the head sphere returns 0, and a vertical ray takes the end-sphere fallback. So a muzzle inside another soldier's torso misses that torso. The in-game effect is not measured.
rows.v2_note: Keep the closed-form tests: they are small, allocation-free and easy to port. Fix the inside-start case so the capsule behaves like the sphere (a hit at t=0), and add unit tests with exact cases, which legacy never had. These tests need the same results on Wasm and native, so pick f32 or f64 once and test against the same fixtures on both.
rows.reason: Hit maths the authoritative v2 simulation decides.

rows.system: Batch ray versus all static colliders (rayStatics)
rows.what: One loop tests a ray against every live static box (axis-aligned or rotated), with the slab test written inline. It returns the nearest hit closer than a maximum distance, or with anyHit the first one found, and writes the normal and distance into a reused array. A NaN ray counts as blocked only when maxT is NaN as well (as in hasLOS with a NaN end point, and only if at least one live static exists); with a finite maxT, a NaN ray misses everything.

rows.what: A pure query that never changes the world. It casts a shot ray against every live soldier (head, torso and legs), skipping the shooter and, unless friendly fire is on, the shooter's team. Then it tests the static colliders and a flat ground plane, and returns the nearest hit: point, normal, kind, id and body part. The result object is reused on every call. The result record is the contract between the SIM and the game: t, hit point (px, py, pz), unit normal (nx, ny, nz), kind, id, part and mult. kind is one of none, enemy (any soldier, teammates included), building, harvester or block (the ground plane and every other static: crates, walls, platforms, ramps, houses, cover, trees and props). id is the SOLDIERS slot for enemy, the buildings[] index for building, the harvesters[] index for harvester, and -1 for block and none. The game maps a hit back by kind and id (SOLDIERS[r.id], buildings[r.id], harvesters[r.id]) and re-checks team there.

Callers: shamble-game.js:1126 (updateAim hover query), 1309 (_jugFirePilot, Juggernaut), 1489 (castShot), 1625 (enemyFire via _botFireWorld, game:1610), 2869 (torque-bow bolts in update()). The ids are set by syncSimWorld: soldier slots game:1446-1448, building id=i game:1450, block id=-1 game:1451 (and 1454-1460), harvester id=i game:1453. rows.v2_note: Keep the pure, read-only design. The comment at core:1491-1492 says it exists so the server can run it against a rewound snapshot for lag compensation, but no rewind is built. Keep one hit world for every shooter (STATUS.md:68, K1). Today bots use _botFireWorld, a view without ramp slots, until ramps become slopes. Keep the team filter, but the server must repeat the team allow-list (STATUS.md:68). Known gaps: the ground is one flat plane (VISION_V2 §6.2 wants a true 3D world with ledges and interiors); kind is 'enemy' for any soldier hit, teammates included when friendly fire is on; only players are swept, with no broad phase (5.4 KB per shot at 48 in JS). How the aim ray is made at height is LOOP_V2 §9 [OPEN]. Keep the idea of a small typed hit result, but make kind an enum and give every static a stable entity id: today every block is id -1, so a hit cannot name which crate, wall or prop it struck, which destructible pieces and replicated hit events will need.
rows.reason: Server-authoritative shot resolution, core of the v2 sim. The aim-at-height input rule is pending LOOP_V2 [OPEN] (§9).

rows.what: A single global object holds the hit world: a list of player records (id, position, alive, stance, team), a list of static colliders (kind, id, alive, box bounds, optional rotation) and a ground height. The game rebuilds it from the live Three.js scene, normally at most once per sim step before shots (frame guard, game:1444). Forced re-syncs come after the player's movement, before the bolts (game:2862), after roster changes (invalidation, game:778), and from the editor's cover-map overlay (shamble-editor.js:564).

Drop the global singleton (a classic-script workaround) and the per-shot rebuild from scene objects. The stance field exists but is always 0 (game:1447-1448).

rows.what: Two one-line helpers that return the length of a 2D or 3D vector with a square root. They replaced Math.hypot, which allocates in V8, across the hot paths.
rows.where: shamble-core.js:743 hyp2(a,b), :744 hyp3(a,b,c), outside the fence but used inside it at core:1508 and core:1544. Used on 2 more core lines (323, 876) and 21 game lines (grep by line); the editor was not converted and still has 9 Math.hypot calls.
rows.evidence: AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md:71-72 (CS2): all 25 Math.hypot calls in core and game were rewritten to hyp2/hyp3 by AST, and allocation fell from 8.0 to about 6.3 MB/s (A/B, noise +/-0.5). AUDIT_BUGS_PERF.md:25 (P1): Math.hypot was 12.5 % of the original GC churn (the code comment at core:741 calls it 'the #1 source', but the audit puts updateOcclusion and updateSoldierAnim higher at 17 %).
rows.v2_note: In Rust use the vector type's length (no allocation question). Lesson for the TypeScript client: Math.hypot allocated in V8 hot paths here, so measure it before using it per frame. Avoid unguarded sqrt of NaN: a NaN length makes hasLOS's maxT NaN, which rayStatics then reports as blocked (if any live static exists), while a NaN direction with a finite range silently misses.
rows.reason: A V8-only workaround; Rust has native vector lengths, and the TS client just needs the lesson.

rows.what: A comment fence marks the bottom of core as a pure maths block with no THREE or DOM use, kept contiguous so it can be lifted out whole for a later headless simulation (Phase 6). The file header and MODULE_MAP point to it. The block is in fact free of THREE and DOM, but it is not self-contained: BODY reads CHAR_DEFAULT from the character recipe higher up in core, resolveShot and hasLOS call hyp3 from outside the fence, hasLOS reads the global SIM instead of taking the world as an argument, and the VIEW-to-SIM bridge comment and the SIM global sit inside the fenced range. The two lists of what the fence holds disagree: the core header omits rayStatic and rayStatics, MODULE_MAP omits BTN and makeInputCommand.

Dependencies that cross the fence: core:1482 BODY={...CHAR_DEFAULT.hit} (CHAR_DEFAULT at core:421), hyp3 core:744 used at core:1508 and :1544, hasLOS core:1544 reads SIM.statics.
rows.evidence: none recorded (no report measures or tests the fence). Code read: a grep of core:1474-1544 for THREE, document, window, Math.random, performance and Date finds only the two comment lines that name THREE, so the block is pure of THREE and DOM. MODULE_MAP.md:122-124 states core is not headless-runnable today and that the lift-out is future work.
rows.v2_note: Keep the idea: the simulation lives behind a hard boundary that has no rendering or browser dependency, so the same code runs in the browser and on the server. In v2 that boundary is the Rust simulation crate compiled to Wasm and native (V2_PHASE0_BRIEF.md:7 and :121, R1; repository layout as a Cargo workspace, :125, R5), enforced by the compiler instead of a comment. Learn from the leaks here: shape data (BODY) came from the visual recipe, helpers came from outside the block, and one query read a global. In v2 the sim owns its own data and every query takes the world as an argument. The JS lift-out itself is not worth doing.
rows.reason: A comment convention for a JavaScript lift-out that v2 replaces with the Rust simulation crate boundary; the contents are marked row by row (CS1-CS10).

rows.system: Team structures, enterable barracks, the map resupply terminal and the map spawn
rows.what: makeBuilding builds a destructible team building as a box body with an accent trim band, a type label and a world health bar: HQ, refinery, power plant, or a plain 'barracks' box (the K glyph in the Cabana grid). It registers it in the buildings array with health from T, a world box and an editor tag. makeBarracks builds the enterable barracks: five addBox walls with a door gap (so they are ordinary obstacles), a lintel, a floor, a roof with its own cloned transparent material so it can fade, a BARRACKS label, and an ARMORY panel on the back wall whose panelPos is where the player opens the shop (nearPanel, 2.6 m). Colours come from the team's relation to PLAYER_TEAM; teamless stays red (buildings) or grey (barracks). One resupply terminal and one map spawn point per map are globals, built and placed by buildMap and saved by serializeMap.

rows.v2_note: LOOP_V2 §2 [DECIDED]: everyone spawns inside their own barracks, in front of the buy terminal, with 3 s of spawn protection and no enemy entry to a barracks interior [DEFAULT]. So the single map-wide resupply terminal and mapSpawn do not survive: each team's barracks carries its terminal and spawn. LOOP_V2 §8 [DEFAULT]: destroying an HQ is a points swing, not an elimination (legacy checkEnd ends the round on it, GE12). §3 keeps refinery deliveries and power-plant pricing; §9 marks other enterable structures [LATER]. Keep: structures as typed map data with team, type, health and transform; health, damage and destruction decided by the Rust sim; barracks walls as real colliders. Avoid: two different things called barracks (a destructible box type and the enterable makeBarracks); a new geometry and material per building and per panel; colour baked from PLAYER_TEAM at build time (v2 colours from the viewer's team on the client, see GW1); the roof fade by per-barracks material clone (GW17). Shapes and colours wait for the look brief.
rows.reason: LOOP_V2 §2 moves spawning and the buy terminal into each team's barracks and §8 turns HQ destruction into a points swing; structure health and colliders go to the Rust sim, the builders to the client.

rows.system: Animation tuning table and critically damped spring
rows.what: One data object holds every animation knob: gait (duty, pelvis drop, lift, cadence bounds), spring stiffnesses, carry / ADS / sprint hold poses per hold style (rifle, smg, scatter; each gun picks one through its GUN_KIT hold), reload choreography keys, and action poses (flinch, death, draw, bayonet charge, throw, shield, katana). An analytic critically damped spring smooths most blended values and stays stable at any frame time (velocity and throw wind-up use their own exponential smoothing, lines 279 and 370). Module-level scratch vectors, quaternions and arrays are reused every frame so the layer itself allocates no math objects.
rows.where: shamble-game.js:132-193 const ANIM (hold 153-163, reload 172-177, actions 179-185, aim 187-191); shamble-game.js:197 springStep; scratch pools _aV/_aQ 231 (10 Vector3 + 10 Quaternion), _aE/_aY/_aDn/_aKnee 232, _aPoleR/_aPoleL/_aHold 233, _aRk 237; helpers _aLerp 234, _aWrap 235, _aSmooth 236, _aKeys 238-239, _aNeutral 240

rows.reason: Client-side cosmetic tuning data plus a stable smoothing helper, worth keeping in shape.

rows.system: Locomotion core: velocity, hip yaw and gait cadence
rows.what: Derives each soldier's velocity from its position change (teleports re-plant), computes walk/run/sprint weights, turns the hips toward movement within a twist budget (backpedal keeps hips to the aim, no flip), and sizes stride and cadence from the legs' real reach at the current crouch height.

rows.reason: Cosmetic locomotion driven purely by replicated position; the sim never reads it.

rows.what: Each foot is planted in the world, swinging along an arc to the next foothold, or doing a timed step. Swings move relative to the moving stance spot so a foot never trails. Catch-up steps fire when a planted foot is left out of reach, and idle re-steps fire when standing turns stray a foot (turn in place). While the soldier is airborne (st.grounded false) both feet are tucked 0.18 m above the root, pitched 0.25 rad, and re-planted on landing.

Known limit: feet plant at the root's height (baseY = g.position.y), with no ground sampling, so slopes and steps are not followed; v2 should sample the terrain height. The airborne tuck needs a replicated grounded flag per soldier from the sim's vertical state. ANIMATION_PLAN.md §8 item 5 plans to reuse it for the Juggernaut walker.
rows.reason: Cosmetic foot placement; port its logic and add terrain sampling.

rows.system: Pelvis motion, leg IK and procedural ankle roll
rows.what: Bobs, sways and rolls the pelvis, lowers it into a running crouch, and caps its height so both feet stay reachable. Then solves each leg onto its foot's ankle point and holds the boot flat, turned with the foot, rolling toe-off and heel-strike in the swing.

rows.reason: Cosmetic leg posing, measured and Brave-confirmed.

rows.system: Gun-first weapon stance and hand IK onto gun sockets
rows.what: Places the gun's stock first, blending carry / ADS / sprint holds per GUN_KIT hold style. It then adds turn sway and bob by gun mass, recoil along the barrel, the weapon-draw lift and the bayonet-charge thrust. The trigger hand solves onto the grip socket and the support hand slides along the rail to the furthest point it can reach.

rows.system: Per-frame animation driver and its input contract
rows.what: Every frame, the player and every alive bot fill one shared state struct (aim yaw, clock, kick, reload dip, reload progress, throw charge, bayonet lean, grounded, ADS, draw timer) and call updateSoldierAnim. Bots pass no kick, reload, throw or draw. Aim pitch travels outside the struct: pitchWeapon writes the gun's rotation.x, and updateSoldierAnim spots a fresh value by comparing it with the value it stored after last frame's posing, then feeds it into the carry and ADS pitch. Nothing culls or simplifies animation for distant or off-screen soldiers.

rows.reason: Ability effects (block, speed, one-hit kills) change combat outcomes, so the sim decides them; LOOP_V2 §4 adds the Tech 1 gate.

rows.what: A charged throw spawns a grenade that falls under gravity, bounces on the ground and explodes after 1.5 s (Molotov 1.4 s). The blast damages soldiers within 6.5 m with linear falloff (owner takes 0.5x, teammates spared unless friendly fire is on), enemy buildings within R+4 and harvesters within R+3, each only when blastReaches finds no blocker. You carry up to T.grenadeMax (3) grenades; a throw needs one and spends it.

rows.what: The time since your last hit counts up each frame; after T.regenDelay (3.5 s) without a hit, your health climbs at T.regenRate (16 HP/s) up to your max health. A hit resets the timer in applyDamage; resupply, respawn and round reset set it to 99 so regen starts at once. Bots do not regenerate.

rows.evidence: Code read: grep regenDelay/regenRate gives only shamble-core.js:77 and shamble-game.js:2700 (player only, no bot path). Values listed in LEGACY_TUNING.md:126-127. No measurement recorded.
rows.v2_note: LOOP_V2 does not mention health regeneration, so whether v2 keeps it (and for bots and humans alike) is a design question for Mustafa. If kept: one rule for every soldier in the sim, delay and rate as data, the timer reset by the server's damage event. The HUD write inside the tick belongs to the client.
rows.reason: Health is authoritative sim state; regen decides who survives the next fight.

rows.system: Bot roles, siege and objective behaviour
rows.what: With no visible target, a bot acts by role, cycled per team slot (push, objective, hunt). Objective bots walk to the active Tech Box while their team doesn't hold it, and otherwise behave like push bots. Push bots head for the nearest live structure of their push team (rotated on each respawn; any other active team when that team has no live building), but still take another team's truck when it is nearer than that building and within 42 m. Hunt bots go for other teams' trucks first. Bots stop 15 m from a building or 13 m from a truck and fire at it, dealing a flat 11 damage with no hit test. Objective and siege walking uses the plain 4.2 m/s, without the unit's speedMult that combat movement applies.

rows.system: Bot verticality: climb steering, jumps and collision

A bot jumps when the ground 1.5 m ahead is above a step but within jump reach. Then it is clamped to the arena, pushed out of obstacles at radius 0.7 m, and given gravity.

rows.what: Builds a 2 m grid over the arena when a match deploys. A cell is blocked when a test circle at its centre (bot radius 0.7 m plus half a cell) gets pushed by the same collision the bots use. The grid arrays are allocated once and reused.

A blocked start or goal moves to the nearest open cell. The search gives up after 8,000 expansions. The path is string-pulled with a grid line-of-sight test, up to 24 cells ahead, into at most 64 waypoints.

The warm-up exists only to stop V8 deoptimising navPath, so drop it in Rust.

rows.system: Route following, replanning and route budget
rows.what: navSteer walks a bot straight when the grid line to its goal is clear. Otherwise it follows a cached route, skipping waypoints it can see. It replans when it has no route, when the goal has moved more than 3 m, every 1.5 s, or when the bot has moved under 0.35 m in 0.8 s. At most 2 searches run per update across all bots.

For route following in general, the same report's paired walks after the wedge fix (clearance and open start cell, not a replan change): stalls of 3 s or more 1-16 per set to 0, direction reversals 226-1,048 to 0-22. three-teams-core report: route denials 52-57 % at 48 soldiers. STATUS: replan storm queued as bot-replan-storm.
rows.v2_note: Known bug: the replan storm (LOOP_V2 §10 says to fix it before uplinks, because moving objectives will make bots replan constantly; §11 step 4). Found in code: NAV.budget is reset on every update() call (2671), so route searches per second grow with frame rate, unlike the sight budget, which counts game time. In Rust, give it a budget per tick and a queue of fair requests, and hysteresis on the clear/blocked switch.
rows.reason: Bot navigation is decided by the authoritative sim and LOOP_V2 keeps it (with the replan-storm fix).

rows.system: FX pool and transient combat effects
rows.what: Short-lived world effects: tracers, muzzle flashes, impact sparks by surface, shell casings, explosions, grenade blast (shock rings, dust, shrapnel, scorch, scuffs), the concussion overlay and the camera kick. Every effect is drawn from per-kind pools of meshes that are built once, and one fx[] loop fades them and returns them to the pool.

TECHNICAL:117: bot-shot FX are skipped beyond TUNE.fx.botCullR 50 m. Code read at 48ffb51 found a live bug at 1050: a `//` comment swallows the rest of the line, so pooled scuffs never get their scale, rotation or position.
rows.v2_note: Keep the pool-per-kind design with caps, and keep the fade curves as data (LOOP_V2 §7 feel kit: muzzle flash, tracer and impact per weapon). Avoid three things: the swallowed-comment bug at 1050 (scuffs show at a stale or origin transform, standing upright); the grenade flash, still a new SphereGeometry and Material per blast (1082); and fx.splice per expiry. The camera kick and concussion stay client-only and must never feed aim. The bot FX cull uses a random sequence that depends on the camera (three-teams-core report l.77), so in v2 the cull must not touch simulation randomness.
rows.reason: Cosmetic client effects. The pooling technique carries over; the look is pending.

rows.what: Keyboard and mouse listeners write a keys{} map plus mouse NDC and button flags. Hard-coded keys: WASD, Shift, Space, R (reload, or restart the round after game over), F, G, E, 1/2/3, Tab, Esc/P, the backquote key and '['. Middle mouse orbits the camera, the right button aims (hold or toggle). Inputs are released when the tab is hidden, and text selection, drag and the context menu are suppressed. The reticle DOM is placed once per frame, not per mousemove.

rows.what: Turns WASD into a move vector relative to the camera yaw, applies sprint (drains stamina; when it runs out, sprint locks until the bar refills to 30 %), ADS, banzai and shield speed multipliers, then smooths the velocity, clamps to the arena and resolves collision. Also drives the stamina bar.

rows.v2_note: Keep as data: STAM values, sprintMult per unit, adsMoveMult, shieldMoveMult, accel. The sim should get a world-space move direction (the client applies the camera yaw), because today's axes depend on camYaw (2751). The velocity lerp 1-exp(-accel*dt) assumes a variable dt, so in v2 it runs at the fixed tick. LOOP_V2 has no sprint or stamina rule, so these are legacy starting values. The stamina bar is HUD (GP10). Collision and vertical movement are owned by GW13/GW14.

rows.what: An isometric follow camera: a screen-space dead zone before the camera pans or looks ahead, smoothed middle-mouse yaw, ADS reaction ('pitch' flattens the view toward the crosshair, 'pan' is a Foxhole-style distance pan that keeps the player on screen), and FOV easing plus recoil, shake and a spring-damped concussion kick. Aim is cast through the stable camera base, so shake never moves the crosshair's world aim.

rows.system: Dev panel, camera style presets and perf overlay
rows.what: A panel toggled with the backquote key. It holds cheats (god mode, infinite ammo, freeze AI, heal, +1000 credits, harvester payout, tech-box tech, +20 tech for us or the enemy, era, silo, unlock all weapons, XP, next level, max level, prestige, reset, kill all, win, lose), live camera sliders (boom, height, FOV, pitch override, ADS-camera mode cycle), five camera presets (Classic, Tactical, Iso, Iso+, Foxhole), halftone sliders, and a map-size slider that resizes the arena (setMapSize). Its perf overlay samples raw frame deltas every frame and shows FPS, average and max frame time, renderer.info draw calls, triangles, geometries, textures, programs and JS heap four times a second, and stays idle while the panel is closed.

DEV.enabled is true in the player build, so anyone can open the cheats with the backquote key. Under server authority, cheats become server or admin commands, never client writes. LOOP_V2 §7 plans a small Feel Lab for live weapon tuning, which should replace the slider half. The preset comments call Iso+ (4) the 'tuned default', but the code defaults to and resets to Iso (3).

rows.what: All sound is generated at runtime from oscillators and noise buffers: shots per weapon, an AMK sniper report (saturated noise layers plus a convolution street echo), reload clicks, steps, clanks, impact thwacks (throttled to one per 55 ms), positional enemy shots and booms (inverse-distance gain, stereo pan against the camera's right axis), the headshot thunk, the kill tick, a looping ambient bed, and the war-room stamp and typewriter sounds. The AudioContext is created and resumed on the first pointer or key press.

rows.v2_note: Keep the no-assets synthesis recipes, the cached AMK noise, shaper and impulse response, the impact throttle and the positional bus. Fix one waste: most calls build a fresh AudioBuffer and fill it in a JS loop on every shot (sfxShot 2230, sfxBoom, sfxEnemyShot); only the AMK and the war-room sounds cache theirs. Pre-build the noise buffers. Distance gain is measured from the player while pan uses the camera, so v2 should use a proper listener. LOOP_V2 §7 puts sound in the per-weapon feel kit as data.

rows.what: Two near-identical HTML pages boot the game: index.html (player build) and editor.html (authoring build). They share one head and one DOM, which must be edited identically by hand. The global reset (*) turns off text selection and touch callouts; #app and the canvas hide the system cursor (cursor:none).

rows.v2_note: Keep the rule that the player build never loads editor code (EDITOR_V2 §5). Avoid two hand-synced copies of the head and DOM. v2 should have one TypeScript client with build-time entries (player, editor) that share component code. Today the editor DOM and Character Lab DOM ship inside index.html as unused weight (see PG9, PG14, PG17).
rows.reason: Two hand-duplicated pages exist only because of classic scripts and file://. A bundled TypeScript client with separate entries replaces them.

rows.system: Design tokens and the two UI families
rows.what: CSS custom properties hold the palette and fonts. The page has three sets: the legacy tokens (paper, ink, olive, brass, friend/hostile, a monospace font), the wr- war-room tokens (paper, manila, olive, red, ink, kit, desk, faded, plus stencil, typewriter and hand fonts) and the editor's own --ed-* set (dark blue-grey, scoped to #editor). The CS14 rule splits screens into a paper family (menu-context screens) and a dark field-kit family (overlays on the live game).

rows.what: Keeps scratch, secrets and personal overrides out of git, and makes every machine see the same bytes. .gitignore excludes node_modules/, the verifier and reviewer scratch folder .gate/, dist/, .env and .env.* (except .env.example), logs, and the local-only kit overrides: .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/agent-memory-local/, .claude/claude-security-guidance.local.md and CLAUDE.local.md. They sit beside the committed settings.json, claude-security-guidance.md and CLAUDE.md, so a personal override never reaches other sessions. .gitattributes forces LF line endings in the repo and working tree (Windows, Linux CI and every agent) and marks images, zip and woff2 as binary.
rows.where: .gitignore:1-11 (.gate/ :2, .env :4-6, local kit overrides :8-11); .gitattributes:1-9 (LF rule :1-2, binary types :3-9)
rows.evidence: docs/reports/2026-10-13-repo-root.md:6 (before the move, .gitignore/.gitattributes covered only the subtree), :13 (b23a133 moves them to the root as pure renames), :29-30 ('git check-ignore matches .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/agent-memory-local/, tools/node_modules/, .gate/, .env, CLAUDE.local.md'). Both files unchanged from 48ffb51 to HEAD (git diff --stat empty). No line-ending incident is recorded.
rows.v2_note: Keep: LF everywhere (Mustafa works on Windows, CI on Linux), .env ignored with an .env.example allowed, local overrides for settings and memory kept out of git, one scratch folder for agents. Add for v2: Rust and Wasm build outputs (target/, the wasm-pack pkg/ output) and the TypeScript build and test caches, decided with the v2 repository layout (R5). Server secrets stay out of the repo (security baseline R6). Avoid ignoring the committed project agent memory (see KT20).
rows.reason: The rules carry over, but the ignore list must follow the v2 toolchain and repository layout.

rows.what: Five agents set 'memory: project' so that they keep notes across sessions: the advisor, the art-director (calibration notes, for example how headless renders differ from Brave), the netcode-architect (earlier decisions), the perf-auditor (baselines with date, commit and numbers) and the security-auditor (threat model, accepted risks). The verifier and docs-keeper have none. Each memory agent is told to check its memory first and, except the advisor and netcode-architect, to save to it afterwards.
rows.where: At 48ffb51: .claude/agents/advisor.md:8; art-director.md:7 (memory), :13 (check first), :33 (save calibration); netcode-architect.md:7, :11; perf-auditor.md:7, :12, :33 (save baselines); security-auditor.md:7, :11, :34 (record threat model); tools lines :4 (no Write for advisor, art-director, perf-auditor, security-auditor); .gitignore:9 (.claude/agent-memory-local/)
rows.evidence: No memory folder is committed at 48ffb51 or at HEAD (git ls-tree). docs/reports/2026-10-14-editor-undo-ground.md:57: 'Calibration notes and baselines were not saved to agent memory (reviewers are read-only).' Baselines live in STATUS.md's health table instead (KT16). kit-v3-0 report :181 keeps .claude/** writable because agent memory lives there. At HEAD (after kit-v3-0) eleven agent files set memory: project, and all of them except the advisor have Write in their tools line (advisor.md:4).
rows.v2_note: Learn: at 48ffb51 the memory was configured but never written, because four of the five memory agents (all but the netcode-architect) had no Write tool, so nothing persisted between reviews. If v2 relies on agent memory for baselines and threat models, check after the first reviews that it is written and committed; otherwise keep baselines in the STATUS health table, which names source, date and method. Changed by kit-v3-0 (agents: eleven with memory, Write added to every memory agent except the advisor).
rows.reason: kit-v3-0 already changes the agents and their tools; whether memory or STATUS holds the baselines is a v2 process choice.
